Oxford Bookworms · Starter · 250 Headwords

Sally's Phone

by Christine Lindop

Story Introduction

Do you have a phone? Who do you call? Who calls you? Can you live without your phone?

Sally has a phone, and a busy life. She gets many phone calls – mostly from her boyfriend, Andrew. Andrew likes telling Sally what to do – and what to wear.

Sally and Andrew are going to a party tonight. 'Wear your blue skirt', says Andrew. But Sally can't wear it – it's dirty, so she has to go shopping for a new one.

But when Sally goes shopping she gets more than just a new skirt – she gets something that will change her life.

🔥 Warm Up — Before You Read

Think about these questions before starting the story:

  • Do you use your phone every day? What do you use it for?
  • Can you live without your phone for one day?
  • Look at the cover. Where is Sally? What is she doing?
  • What do you think will happen in the story?
Chapter 1

Morning

Pages 1–5 · Sally's day begins

🔥 Warm Up

Before reading, look at the illustrations and answer:

  • What time do you think it is?
  • Where is Sally? What is she looking for?

It is Thursday morning. Sally is in bed. Suddenly – Ring ring! Her phone is ringing – but where is it?

Sally gets out of bed and looks in her bag. No phone. She looks under the bed. No phone. Then she looks behind the door. There is her phone. Sally picks up her phone and answers it.

Sally searches for her phone behind the door
Andrew
'Hello Sally, it's Andrew.'

Andrew is Sally's boyfriend. He has got a lot of money and a beautiful and expensive car.

Sally
'Andrew, it's only seven o'clock—'
Andrew
'Don't forget, Sally – we're meeting Michael tonight. It's an important evening, because Michael's my new boss. Wear your blue skirt, Sally, I like that skirt. I must go now. See you at half past six. Bye.'
Sally
'But Andrew . . . Bye.'

'I can't wear the blue skirt,' Sally thinks. 'It's dirty. What can I wear?'

Andrew calls Sally early in the morning

Sally is having breakfast with her mother and her brother Jack.

Sally
'I'm going out tonight. Andrew and I are meeting his new boss.'
Jack
'Andrew?' 'Huh!'
Sally
'Oh be quiet, Jack. Andrew is very nice to me.'
Jack
'Nice?' 'Huh! "Sally, I want a sandwich." "Yes, Andrew." "Sally, I don't like your hair." "No, Andrew, sorry Andrew." "Sally—"'

But then Sally stands up, and Jack runs out of the room.

Breakfast with Mum and Jack

Sally gets on the train. There are a lot of people on the train. Most of them are talking on their phones.

Voice 1
'John? John! Get up and go to work. It's late!'
Voice 2
'Have you got my money? I need it today. I must have it today.'
Voice 3
'Remember – go to the supermarket tonight. Don't forget!'

And Sally is listening to Andrew.

Andrew
'Sally, meet me at six o'clock, not at half past six. OK?'
Sally
'OK Andrew – but my blue skirt—'
Andrew
'I must go, Sally – bye.'
Sally on the train — everyone is on their phones

Then the train goes into a tunnel. The people on the train can not talk on their phones. They must talk to the other people on the train.

Max
'Hello, Graham! How are you?'
Graham
'Oh hello! I'm very well.'
Lucy
'Where are you working now?'
Friend
'I'm in a new office in Bank Street.'
Someone
'Those are nice shoes, Jane.'
Jane
'Thank you, Mary.'

After three minutes, the train comes out of the tunnel. Everyone talks on their phones again.

Voice
'Hello? John? Are you out of bed now?'
The train goes into a tunnel — people talk to each other

Now Sally is at work. She is talking to her friend Claire, and she tells her about Andrew, Michael, and the blue skirt.

Claire
'It's OK, Sally. Let's go out at lunchtime. We can find a new skirt. You can wear it tonight.'

Later, Claire and Sally are having coffee with Louise. She works with them.

Ring ring! It is Andrew again.

Andrew
'Hi, Sally. Look, meet me at the Bar Bogart, not the Cosmo Bar – OK? The Bar Bogart is nearer. Bye.'
Claire
'Bar Bogart. Mmm – that's nice.'
Louise
'Huh! Forget him, Sally. Who needs men? "Do this, do that, go there, don't go there." Huh!'
Sally at work — telling Claire and Louise about Andrew and the blue skirt
⏱ Pause & Think — 5 min

💬 Quick Discussion

  1. What does Andrew tell Sally to wear? Why can't she wear it?
  2. What does Jack think about Andrew?
  3. What happens when the train goes into a tunnel? Is this good or bad?
  4. In your life, do you talk more on the phone or face to face?
Chapter 2

Lunchtime

Pages 6–9 · Shopping and a new meeting

It is one o'clock. Sally and Claire are looking at skirts.

Claire
'Do you like this one, Sally?'
Sally
'Yes, it's beautiful, but I never wear red.'
Claire
'Do you like red?'
Sally
'Yes, I do – but Andrew doesn't.'
Claire
'Well, it's a beautiful skirt. You like red. What do you want to do?'

Sally buys the skirt.

Claire and Sally look at skirts in the shop

Claire goes back to work, but Sally wants a coffee. She goes into a café. She buys a coffee and sits down. Then she phones her mother.

Sally
'Hi, Mum. I've got a new skirt – it's beautiful! I want to wear it tonight.'
Mum
'What colour is it?'
Sally
'It's red.'
Mum
'That's nice. Red is a good colour for you.'
Sally in the café on the phone — Paul nearby with the red bag

Next to Sally, Paul is finishing his coffee. He phones his friend and talks to him. Then he stands up. The bag with the red skirt falls on the floor.

Paul
'Oh! I'm sorry.' (He puts down his phone and picks up the bag.) 'Here's your bag.'
Sally
'That's OK. Thank you.' (She smiles.)

'What a nice smile!' Paul thinks.

Paul picks up his phone and goes out of the café. Sally finishes her coffee. She picks up her bag and her phone, and goes back to work.

Paul picks up Sally's bag and returns it to her
⏱ Pause & Think — 5 min

💬 Quick Discussion

  1. Why does Sally buy the red skirt? Is this a surprise?
  2. What happens in the café between Sally and Paul?
  3. Can you guess? What problem will this cause?
Chapter 3

Afternoon

Pages 10–17 · The wrong phone

Paul is in his office. Ring ring!

'What's that noise?' Paul thinks. He answers the phone. It is Andrew.

Andrew
'Hello, Sally?'
Paul
'It's not Sally, it's Paul.'
Andrew
'Paul? Paul who? Where's Sally?'
Paul
'Who's Sally? There's no Sally here.'
Andrew
'Huh!'

Andrew finishes the call.

Andrew calls Sally's phone — but Paul answers

Paul wants to phone his mother. He finds 'Mum' on the phone, and presses the button.

Paul
'Hello, Mum. It's Paul.'
Voice
'Paul? Who's Paul? I'm not Paul's Mum. I'm Sally's Mum and Jack's Mum.'

'What's happening?' Paul thinks.

Paul
'What number is that?'
Sally's Mum
'It's 0783 491839.'
Paul
'I'm very sorry. It's the wrong number.'
Sally's Mum
'That's OK.' 'What a nice voice!' she thinks.
Paul looks at the phone — it's not his!

Paul talks to a friend at work.

Paul
'This is Sally's phone – and Sally's got my phone.'
Friend
'But who is Sally?'
Paul
'I don't know.'
Friend
'Why don't you phone her?'
Paul
'What's my number? I don't know my number.'
Friend
'Why not?'
Paul
'Because I never call my number!'
Paul tells his friend about the switched phones

Paul phones his mother.

Paul
'Mum, what's the number of my phone?'
Mum
'Why do you want your phone number, Paul?'
Paul
'Because Sally's got my phone.'
Mum
'Who's Sally?'
Paul
'I don't know, but she's got my phone, and I've got her phone.'
Mum
'I don't understand.'
Paul
'I know. It doesn't matter. Have you got my number?'
Mum
'Here it is. 0781 644834.'
Paul
'Thanks, Mum.'
Paul phones his mother to find out his own number

Meanwhile, Sally is at work. Ring ring!

Katharine
'Hello, is Paul there?'
Sally
'No, I'm sorry, this—'
Katharine
'Can you give a message to him? This is his sister Katharine. There's a party at my house tonight. It's my birthday. 8 o'clock – OK? Bye.'
Sally at her desk — Katharine calls with a birthday party message

Sally talks to Claire and Louise.

Sally
'I've got a message for Paul – but who's Paul? Do you know a Paul, Claire?'
Claire
'No. What's the message?'
Sally
'It's his sister Katharine's birthday, and she's having a party tonight. Do you think it's a wrong number?'
Claire
'Yes, I think it is.'
Louise
'Hey Sally! Put on your red skirt and go to the party. Forget Andrew!'
Sally tells Claire and Louise about Paul's message

Paul phones Sally.

Paul
'Hello, Sally – this is Paul.'
Sally
'Paul – are you Katharine's brother?'
Paul
'Yes, that's right. And I've got your phone.'
Sally
'My phone? Oh – wait a minute. The Café Cuba at lunchtime? The bag on the floor?'
The two phones switched at Café Cuba at lunchtime
Paul
'Yes, that's right. Well, we need to change phones.'
Sally
'OK – where are you now, Paul?'
Paul
'In College Road. I work there.'
Sally
'I work in Manchester Street. Can we meet in Queen's Square?'
Paul
'OK. What time do you finish work?'
Sally
'At half past five.'
Paul
'Let's meet in Queen's Square at a quarter to six. Phone me then.'
Sally
'OK, Paul.'
Paul arranges where to meet Sally in Queen's Square
⏱ Pause & Think — 5 min

💬 Quick Discussion

  1. How did the phones get switched?
  2. Why doesn't Paul know his own phone number? Is this funny?
  3. Who is Katharine? What is she inviting Paul to?
  4. What does Louise want Sally to do? Do you agree?
Chapter 4

Evening

Pages 18–24 · The meeting that changes everything

It is half past five. Sally puts on her new skirt.

Sally
'Do you like it, Louise?'
Louise
'Oh yes. It's very nice.'
Sally puts on her new red skirt — Louise loves it!

It is twenty to six. Paul arrives in Queen's Square. He looks for Sally. He can not remember. He phones Sally.

Paul
'Hello, Sally. It's Paul. I'm in Queen's Square.'
Sally
'Hello, Paul. I'm coming.'
Paul and Sally both on phones trying to find each other in the crowded square

There are lots of people in Queen's Square, and many of them are talking on phones. Which is Paul? Sally can not remember. She phones Paul.

Sally
'Paul – have you got black hair?'
Paul
'No, I haven't.'

'Good!' Sally thinks.

Sally
'Have you got a book in your hand?'
Paul
'No, I haven't.'

'Good!' Sally thinks.

Sally
'Where are you, Paul?'
Paul
'I'm near the trees.'

Sally goes across the square to the trees.

Sally
'Are you Paul?'

Paul looks at Sally. 'She's beautiful!' he thinks.

Paul
'Yes, I'm Paul.'

'He's nice!' Sally thinks.

Paul and Sally meet near the trees — both like what they see
Paul
'I'm Sally. So – we meet again.'
Paul
'I'm sorry about your phone, Sally. Here it is.'
Sally
'That's OK. Here's your phone, Paul.'
Paul
'Sally – would you like a drink? I want to say sorry.'
Sally
'OK, but I haven't got much time.'

Paul looks for a bar. 'Let's go to the Blue Moon. We can have a drink there.'

Paul and Sally arrive at the Blue Moon

Paul and Sally are at the Blue Moon. Sally sits down at a table. Paul brings their drinks.

Paul
'Here's your drink, Sally. And I am sorry about your phone.'
Sally
'Forget it, Paul – it doesn't matter. Oh, I've got a message for you. It's from your sister Katharine.'
Paul
'From Katharine? What is it?'
Sally
'She says that it's her birthday today, and there's a party at her house.'
Paul and Sally at the Blue Moon — Sally delivers Katharine's message
Paul
'Oh no! I always forget birthdays. What can I do?'

Sally looks across the square. Near the trees a woman is selling flowers.

Sally
'Buy some flowers for your sister, and take them to the party.'
Paul
'Of course! That's the answer. Look, Sally – do you want to come to the party with me? Katharine always has good parties.'
Paul realises he forgot his sister's birthday!
Sally
'Well, I . . .'
Paul
'Oh, I must tell you. I've got a message for you from Andrew. He says—'
Sally
'It doesn't matter, Paul. I don't want the message. I would like to go to the party with you. But I must do something before we go.'

Sally takes her phone out of her bag and turns it off.

In the Bar Bogart, Andrew phones Sally. Sally does not answer.

Andrew
'Sally?' 'Sally? Answer me!'

Sally and Paul leave the Blue Moon.

Paul
'That's a nice skirt. I like red.'

Sally smiles at him. ✨

Paul and Sally leave together — a new beginning ✨
⏱ Final Discussion — 10 min

💬 After Reading — Think & Talk

  1. Why does Sally turn off her phone at the end?
  2. Is Andrew a good boyfriend? Use examples from the story.
  3. How does a switched phone change Sally's life?
  4. Paul says "I like red." — why is this important?
  5. Do you think Sally and Paul will be together? Why?
Reference

Glossary

Key words from the story

bar
a place where people can buy and have drinks
birthday
the day when your age changes
boss
the person that you work for
boyfriend
a man or boy that a girl likes and goes out with
button
a phone has buttons with numbers on
buy
give someone money for something
coffee
a hot drink
Hi
hello (informal)
lunchtime
the time (usually 12–2 o'clock) when people stop work to eat
message
something you want to tell somebody
party
a meeting of friends to eat, drink, talk, dance etc.
press
push with your finger
ring
make a sound like a bell (a telephone rings)
sell
give someone something and get money for it
turn off
stop something working
voice
you speak and sing with your voice
